verdict.rationale: Bevy is free and open source under the permissive MIT or Apache 2.0 licenses, which allow reading and modifying the code. The vendor frames this as letting developers "fully own their tools" with visibility into the tech they use, and the public GitHub repository and crates.io license metadata ('MIT OR Apache-2.0') independently confirm this. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of a workflow for patching or forking the engine source (e.g. building from a local fork), and hands-on reports of users actually modifying engine internals.
